source_name: IOM Kosovo — diaspora and remittances programme publications
why_relevant: IOM's Kosovo mission publishes diaspora-engagement analysis citing remittance shares of GDP and household receipt rates; useful for triangulating household penetration of remittances (share of families receiving) which maps to cash-withdrawal behaviour.

source_name: World Bank — International mobility as a development strategy: Kosovo Country Report
why_relevant: Country-specific analytical report on Kosovo migration and remittances with source-country structure and channel analysis; a compact, citable baseline for the diaspora-to-cash pipeline.

source_name: diasporafordevelopment.eu — Kosovo country factsheet (EU/ICMPD diaspora programme)
why_relevant: Compact EU-funded factsheet with emigration stock and remittance-to-GDP indicators for Kosovo; convenient pre-aggregated cross-check and a pointer to the wider EU diaspora-programme document set.

source_name: MPBAP — Divizioni për Shërbimet Private të Sigurisë (Division for Private Security Services)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Internal Affairs division that licenses, inspects and revokes licences for private security companies — the regulator of Kosovo's cash-in-transit and ATM-servicing operators. The licence register held here is the route to identifying who physically moves and replenishes cash in Kosovo, an actor set with almost no public commercial visibility.

source_name: SIGAL Kosovë — Sigurimet Financiare / 'Sigurimi i Bankave' (bank and cash-in-transit insurance product page)
why_relevant: Insurer product page covering cash-in-safe and cash-in-transit cover for banks in Kosovo. Insurance product structure and the existence of a dedicated bank/CIT line is an indirect reveal that a commercial cash-transport market exists and of the risk categories it is priced on — one of the few open windows on a sector with no public operator data.

source_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikës së Kosovës (GZK) — Official Gazette / legal act repository
why_relevant: Authoritative full text of Law No. 04/L-093 on Banks, Microfinance Institutions and Non-Bank Financial Institutions (the legal basis for MTO licensing) and of the private-security and payment-system laws. The gazette search is the definitive pointer for tracing any legal change affecting remittance and cash-handling actors.

source_name: kosovofacts.com — Remitencat në Kosovë and licensed financial institutions data pages
why_relevant: Albanian-language data-journalism aggregator that republishes BQK remittance series as tidy multi-year tables and maintains a page on licensed financial institutions. Useful as a fast cross-check and change-detector when BQK's own site is bot-defended, but always re-verify against BQK primary data.

source_name: Serbian-language media coverage of Kosovo remittances (Danas, TRT Balkan, B92)
why_relevant: Serbian-language press reports BQK remittance releases promptly and adds regional comparison (Kosovo vs Serbia vs BiH diaspora inflows). Valuable for the sr-language coverage requirement and for capturing figures reported to Serbian-speaking communities in Kosovo, where cash reliance is high.

source_name: Ministria e Punëve të Jashtme dhe Diasporës (MPJD) — diaspora policy and diaspora registration
why_relevant: The ministry runs the official online diaspora registration (results handed to ASK) and sets diaspora strategy. Registration counts and strategy documents give the population denominator behind remittance flows and signal any policy push from cash remittances toward investment/formal channels.

source_name: KosovaJob.com — Kosovo's largest job portal (banking/cards/payments vacancies)
why_relevant: Bank job ads for card operations, POS/acquiring, payment-systems support name the platforms, channels and volumes a bank operates. Confirmed live listings include 'Zyrtar/Specialist per Operacione me Kartela', 'Zyrtar per mbeshtetje te operimit te sistemeve te pagesave', TEB 'Praktikant te Operacioneve me Kartela / Card Operations Intern', and 'Zyrtar i Larte ne Departamentin e Pagesave'. Dated, cheap, and structurally invisible to statistics-only searches.

source_name: PunaIme.org (part of the KosovaJob network)
why_relevant: Second listing surface of the same network; some employers post here only. Carries data/reporting and payments roles ('Specialist të Raportimit dhe Menaxhimit të të Dhënave') that reveal internal MIS and card-reporting stacks.

source_name: ShpalljePune.com — active Kosovo vacancy aggregator
why_relevant: Independent aggregator of active Kosovo job ads; useful redundancy for bank/PSP vacancies that expire quickly on the primary portals.

source_name: JapPune.com — Kosovo vacancy portal
why_relevant: Third-tier Kosovo job portal; adds coverage of smaller NBFIs, e-money institutions and fintechs whose hiring signals are not carried by the big portals.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo — career / vacancies page
why_relevant: Bank-side primary vacancy feed; ads name the card/ATM/e-banking systems and organisational units, and the appearance/disappearance of card-product roles tracks product roadmaps ahead of any published statistic.

source_name: TEB Sh.A. Kosovo — corporate site (about/management/careers)
why_relevant: TEB is a principal card issuer/acquirer in Kosovo. Its about/management pages name a 'Head of Cards and POS Business' role and its portal ads (card operations interns) confirm in-house card processing — a direct read on who owns POS acquiring capability.

source_name: BQK — Consumer Protection / complaints portal (Mbrojtja e Konsumatorit)
why_relevant: The regulator's complaints division page describes the complaint intake channel (https://ankesat.bqk-kos.org) and the legal basis (Ligji per sistemin e pagesave, Rregullore per trajtimin e ankesave). Complaint categories quantify card/ATM incident rates — a proxy for card and ATM usage intensity.

source_name: BQK — Vendimet e Bordit (Executive/CBK Board decisions notices)
why_relevant: Dated board-decision notices record licensing of banks, e-money and payment-service institutions, registrations, and supervisory/enforcement actions. New PSP/e-money licences are the earliest observable signal of market-structure change in Kosovo payments.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events) — agenda and speaker list
why_relevant: Regional payments conference whose speaker roster includes Kosovo-linked figures (e.g. Linda Shomo, Balkan Fintech Association; Bashkim Zeqiri, Pysera Kosovo). Conference decks and panel descriptions routinely quote transaction volumes, card penetration and acquiring metrics not otherwise published for XK.

source_name: STIKK — Kosovo ICT Association / KosICT Technology Festival
why_relevant: KosICT is Kosovo's largest tech festival (60+ speakers, 2200+ attendees per the association's own account) and regularly features bank/fintech digital-payments sessions. Speaker lists and session titles map who inside Kosovo banks owns payments technology.

source_name: The Banker — Bank of the Year awards, Kosovo category
why_relevant: Award citations are dense with otherwise-unpublished operating metrics: the Kosovo Bank-of-the-Year write-ups have cited robotic process automation for efficiency, a 'customer-focused digital leader' strategy, and 2025 figures of EUR 1.6bn total assets (+10%), deposits +11%, lending +21% for the winner. Award season yields a dated, comparable metric drop.

source_name: Global Finance — Best Bank in Kosovo awards
why_relevant: Second independent annual award naming a Kosovo winner (confirmed 2021, 2022, 2023 citations reproduced by the winning bank). Criteria explicitly include asset growth, profitability, geographic reach and product innovation — i.e. a structured annual metric snapshot of the Kosovo market leader.

source_name: Euromoney Awards for Excellence — Kosovo national winners
why_relevant: A 2026 Kosovo national-winners page exists, giving a third annual award-citation stream. Euromoney citations often quote digital-channel adoption and transaction-growth figures for the winning bank.

source_name: EBRD Trade Facilitation Programme awards — 'Most Active Issuing Bank in Kosovo'
why_relevant: An IFI-issued, volume-based award (NLB Banka Prishtina repeatedly named most active issuing bank in Kosovo) — a rare externally validated ranking of trade-finance/payment activity by institution.

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of Kosovo banks (BKT Kosova, ProCredit Bank Kosova, TEB Sh.A., Raiffeisen Kosovo)
why_relevant: Bank LinkedIn pages announce card/POS product launches, ATM-fleet changes, digital-channel milestones and executive appointments (e.g. a new Head of Channel Management at ProCredit Bank Kosova) well before annual reporting. Executive posts occasionally cite transaction counts.

source_name: Kosovo bank management/board pages (executive roster for payments & cards)
why_relevant: Official management pages are the authoritative seed list for the executive-signal watchlist: they identify who holds retail/cards/digital portfolios (e.g. Head of Retail Banking Group at BKT Kosova, Head of Cards and POS Business at TEB) so LinkedIn and conference monitoring can be targeted rather than speculative.

source_name: Kallxo.com — investigative coverage of complaints against banks
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that has published an analysis titled 'Rriten ankesat ndaj bankave ne Kosove' (complaints against banks are rising) — journalists obtain complaint breakdowns from BQK that are not posted on the regulator's site, making the outlet an effective FOI proxy.

source_name: Telegrafi — Kosovo consumer-complaint and conference reporting
why_relevant: High-volume Kosovo outlet that reports both aggregate consumer-complaint counts (e.g. over 1,000 consumer complaints, led by electricity meters and online purchases) and conference coverage of BQK/fintech events. Useful as a dated, searchable mirror for events and complaint figures that vanish from primary sites.
